newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Mulialand proposes bonds for property.
newsitem.headline: Mulialand proposes bonds for property.

text.p: Indonesia's large property firm PT Mulialand said on Friday its majority stakeholder PT Muliasentra Gunaswakarya has submitted a proposal to the Capital Market Supervisory Agency (Bapepam) to issue exchangeable bonds.

"Yes we have submitted a proposal to Bapepam on Thursday to raise funds through exchangable bonds. But we can't give you any further details as it is still being reviewed by Bapepam," Mulialand's senior official Ronni Djohan told Reuters.
Djohan declined to give further details, saying the proceeds from the bonds would be used to finance its large property project Taman Anggrek II in West Jakarta.
According to several sources, the proceeds were expected to be between 150 billion rupiah and 200 billion rupiah.
Djohan said the Muliasentra's exchangeable bond issuance was proposed as Mulialand was not allowed to issue convertible bonds after making a rights issue in 1996.
He said exchangable bonds were usually issued by the majority stakeholders of listed firms, while convertible bonds were issued by the listed firms themselves.
